argument.p: This argument summarizes the chapter that follows: it introduces the question of the soul's nature, previews the three replies considered, and states the author's conclusion in brief.

div.head: Chapter One: On the Nature of the Soul
div.p: Here begins the discussion. Some hold that the soul is simple and indivisible, while others argue for a composite nature. The term ψυχή itself carries this ambiguity, as does the Latin anima.
The reader is reminded that this claim rests on Genesis 1:27, which speaks of humankind made in the divine image, and again on John 1:1-5 for the nature of the Word.

As one early witness put itThis is an inline note: a brief aside that expands on the surrounding claim without interrupting the main argument for readers who do not need the detail., the question was already old by the time it reached the schools.
Consider the following testimony, offered in verse:

lg.l: The soul that sinneth, it shall die;
the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father,
neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son.
